jobs.title: Data Scientist – Optimization & Control
jobs.description: Role You’ll improve and extend the decision logic behind our battery fleet. Our optimization already runs our batteries every day; now we want to make it sharper, more robust and ready for new use cases. Our batteries sit behind the meter at industrial sites, so every decision has to balance customer savings, grid constraints and market value under uncertainty. Our data scientists and quantitative researchers work as one team and often across each other's topics. What you will do The role covers two closely linked areas. You can work in either one and switch between them as priorities and your interests evolve: Fleet optimization: Plan how each battery runs over the coming hours and days, combining customer savings, grid fee rules and market value within each site's limits. Forecasts of load, PV and prices are generated and fed into the plan, which has to stay robust to their uncertainty. You also measure how much value we actually capture. On-site control: Make the plan work in reality. Within our local control system, you design the logic that executes the schedule at each site, reacts to deviations and falls back safely when data or devices fail, while hard limits such as grid capacity, feed-in restrictions and state of charge always hold. Topics you'll work on You join work that is already running and take ownership of topics as priorities require. These are the areas where we want to add strength: Improving and extending our optimization models for sequential decision-making on time series, across customer savings, grid fee rules and market value. Making decisions more robust to forecast uncertainty (load, PV, prices). Developing the on-site decision logic of our local control system: MPC, constraint handling and fallbacks. Making sure hard constraints always hold in operation: grid connection limits, feed-in restrictions, state of charge.
